summary: The Department of Aeronautics reviewed the draft environmental statement for the Lincoln Highway improvement project and concluded that the proposed development would have no effect on the environment relative to aeronautical users. The agency's position appears twice in the document: once as a paraphrase in the comment-summary table and once as the full letter in Appendix A. In both instances, the department expresses neither support nor opposition, simply noting the project falls outside its area of concern.
complaint_summary: The Department of Aeronautics, in a letter dated April 21, 1972, states that after considering the project under NEPA, it is their opinion that the proposed development will have no effect on the environment relative to aeronautical users.

statement.text:
In accordance with the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969, we have considered the above referenced project as to the environmental effects that might be under our jurisdiction or departmental expertise. It is the opinion of this office that the proposed development will not have any effect upon the environment relative to aeronautical users.
Insofar as this office can determine, the construction of this project will present no adverse long range effect on the operation of facilities under the jurisdiction of this department.

Dear Mr. Ziejewski:
This is in response to your letter of April 14, 1972, requesting the Department of the Interior's comments on the draft environmental/Section 4(f) statement for the proposed upgrading of FA Route 23, Section 22-23-12R of Lincoln Highway from Cicero Avenue to Chicago Road in Cook County, Illinois.
Section 4(f) Comments
From the information presented, we agree that there is no feasible and prudent alternative to the proposed project. The compensation for the right-of-way taken from the yard and playground of the Roosevelt School should be sufficient to provide total payment to the City of Chicago Heights for the portion of Sunnyside Avenue that will be closed to provide replacement land. We would also recommend that the replacement of trees and shrubs and the implementation of other landscaping measures discussed in the Section 4(f) submission be included in the contract plans rather than being included in the right-of-way settlement, if this is agreeable with School District No. 170. If these recommendations and the proposals outlined in the draft Section 4(f) submission are carried out, then we believe that this compensation and replacement will adequately offset the loss of playground.
Environmental Statement Comments
The statement contains no mention of any consideration given to historical values that might be affected by the proposal nor is there any indication of consultation with the State Liaison Officer for Historic Preservation. The final environmental impact statement should point out whether any historic sites will be affected along with giving evidence of consultations with the State Liaison Officer for Historic Preservation, who is the Director, Department of Conservation, 102 State Office Building, 400 South Spring Street, Springfield, Illinois 62706.

Because at least one stream (Thorn Creek) will be crossed, the final environmental impact statement should contain a discussion of the impact of the project on the stream and life systems associated with the creek and measures to be taken to reduce damage. We also recommend that a thorough study be made to determine the appropriate sizes for the water structures at stream crossings in this project. The final statement should reflect the results of this study which can, in part, be based on data stemming from the Geological Survey's crest stage gages on the streams of the project area.
Contingent upon implementation of the measures to minimize harm as reflected in the Section 4(f) material, the Department of the Interior would have no objection to approval of the Section 4(f) aspects of the project by the Secretary of Transportation.
Sincerely yours,
Deputy AssistantSecretary of the Interior

Dear Mr. Ziejewski:
We have completed our review of the Draft Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) for the proposed widening of Lincoln Highway, Cicero Avenue to Chicago Road, Cook County, Illinois, as requested in your letter of April 14, 1972. The following comments are for your use in preparing the Final EIS.
Noise
Since this project involves the widening of an existing highway in an area of extensive development, a noise exposure survey should be undertaken to determine if the closer proximity of traffic lanes and increase number of vehicles will have a detrimental effect on any existing land uses. Procedures should be in accordance with PPM 90-2.
Air Pollution
The region is classified Priority I with respect to all major pollutants. It is thus important that no significant decline in air quality results in the immediate area of the project either during or after construction.
As mentioned on page 26, debris from the project should be disposed of by means other than open burning. The destruction of some 14 buildings should be accomplished while keeping fugitive dust emissions to a minimum by use of water applications. One site asphaltic or concrete batching plants should be equipped with adequate emission control devices.
Although the EIS discusses the project from a traffic decongestion standpoint, it fails to provide adequate information to assess the resulting ambient air quality. Information required would be average route speed for peak and non-peak hours before and anticipated after completion of the project. Then the inverse relationships of Compilation of Air Pollution Emission Factors, AP-42, describing carbon

Mr. Sigmund C. Ziejewski Illinois Division of Highways
monoxide and hydrocarbon emission factors as a function of speed, can readily be applied.
It is felt that inclusion of the above information in the Final Impact Statement will allow a more comprehensive evaluation of the project's impact on air quality in the immediate area.
Solid Waste
Disposal of the condemned buildings, existing pavement and associate highway debris should be in accordance with State of I Illinois requirements. If known, the disposal site should be indicated in the EIS.
We appreciate the opportunity to review this Draft EIS and apologize for the delay in returning these comments.
Sincerely yours,
Donald A. Wallgren
Acting Chief, Federal Activities
Coordination Branch

"-UNITED STATES GOVERNMENT
Memorandum
OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY
MAY 3 1 1972
Draft Environmental Impact Statement: Highway Project F-239(), I.D. 05-11-72-16, Sections
SUBJECT: 22-23-12 R, FA Route 23, US-30 (Lincoln Highway)
Cook County, Illinois
refer to TEU-12
Acting Assistant Secretary for Environment and Urban Systems
C. S. Monnier, Division Engineer Springfield, Illinois
We appreciate the opportunity to review and comment on this draft environmental impact statement. We would suggest that the final statement document the following:
1. Input from agencies or staff with relocation expertise on whether any problems are likely to arise with respect to replacement housing.
2. It is suggested that the final statement provide documentation of alternatives to the use of 4(f) lands, such as utilizing the other side of Lincoln Highway for the widening.
3. More description of efforts to minimize harm to the playground would be helpful, including whether the existing ballfields will be preserved or replaced.
4. It would be helpful to have the final statement reflect coordination of the project with the Department of Housing and Urban Development and the Department of the Interior on the Section 4(f) lands.
We look forward to receiving the final environmental impact statement and proposed Section 4(f) determination, including the comments received from other public agencies and the general public on the draft statement.
John E. Hirten
Acting Assistant Secretary
